records.note: Tall gray backed bench has coherent posts, crossbars and legs. Blue slats sit above gray seat and overhang; two nearby levels visible in sections. The relation could be a thin upper seat cap or redundant floating plane, so adoption remains uncertain; visible gap is not inferred from mesh indices.

Complete low gray slatted bench with multiple braced supports is visible under a floating blue slat group. Obliques and front/side sections separate blue seating level from lower gray seat; C does not serve as the actual seating surface.

A coherent gray slab bench with end-panel supports stands above the blue C patch. Both sections separate gray seating surface from the low blue patch; C projects laterally below it rather than serving the seat. A clear C/body gap is visible, without resolved folded gray debris.

Gray back and end legs remain, but the seating region has broad open gaps and separated rails. The blue patch projects from an intermediate height and does not complete the lower gray seating level; obliques and side section show a misaligned stack rather than natural adoption.

Blue slat seat floats above a low gray distorted shell/back assembly. Left gray panels separate, and the base/support outline has broken triangular ends. Front section places the gray seat far below C; side view shows unsupported offset layered surfaces rather than an organized bench around C.

Recognizable gray slab bench has two end-panel supports. Broad gray triangles overlay most blue seat slats and produce another top plane just above C, confirmed by the side section. Blue is visible only through diagonal strips; this is competing coverage, not a clean adoption of the complete slatted surface. No separate gray debris clearly resolved.

Gray pedestal bench has two firm supports and a plank top. Blue C is hidden inside the board volume; side section crosses the middle of gray board walls below their upper faces. Coherent shape but the seating surface supersedes C; no clear detached fragments.

Gray backed bench with panel back and complete end legs has its seating frame far below blue C. Reverse oblique and side section show the blue plate suspended midway up the back, with an empty gap and another gray seat below.

Gray bench has raised end panels and a coherent slab seat, but blue C lies beneath that seat. Both sections resolve the gray upper surface above C. End panels show visible ragged gaps; supports are present. C is covered by a competing seat rather than acting as its seating top.

Both obliques show a complete gray plank bench on two end supports, while the blue condition plate is suspended well below the gray seating top. The same separated heights appear in both fixed sections. Shape and supports remain plausible, but C is not adopted; an obvious C/body gap remains.
